Here's the complete solution for turning a Flox environment into a Docker container image.

## Manifest

Add a `[containerize.config]` section to your `.flox/env/manifest.toml`. This is optional — `flox containerize` works on any environment as-is — but the config lets you set the runtime command, ports, user, etc. for the image:

```toml
version = 1

[install]
# whatever your environment already has, e.g.:
# python3.pkg-path = "python311"

# Optional: shape the resulting image

user = "appuser"               # run as non-root (username or "uid:gid")
exposed-ports = ["8080/tcp"]   # ports the image documents/exposes
cmd = ["python", "app.py"]     # default command (runs inside the activated env)
working-dir = "/app"
volumes = ["/data"]            # mount points for persistent data
labels = { version = "1.0" }
```

If you omit `[containerize.config]`, the image defaults to an interactive shell with the environment activated.
